items.claim: A reflected XSS in a subdomain's parameter can be used to make an authenticated same-site request to the parent origin's account endpoint, so the impact of a subdomain XSS is measured by whether sensitive account data or an API key comes back.
items.body:
A reflected XSS in a subdomain's parameter can be used to make an authenticated same-site request to the parent origin's account endpoint, so the impact of a subdomain XSS is measured by whether sensitive account data or an API key comes back.

HackTricks reference: 6ef0efec (notion:6ef0efec-1585-4209-9215-06befb8148f9)
items.disproof: The vulnerable subdomain's script is blocked from making the cross-origin authenticated request, or the response carries no credential-bearing account data, so no API key is recoverable.

Stored XSS exploits occur when an attacker injects dangerous content into a data store that is later read and included in dynamic content. From an attacker’s perspective, the optimal place to inject malicious content is in an area that is displayed to either many users or particularly interesting users. Interesting users typically have elevated privileges in the application or interact with sensitive data that is valuable to the attacker. items.claim: A working XSS sink can be proven with a payload that ships the victim's document.cookie to an attacker-controlled server, giving the tester an out-of-band confirmation rather than a visual alert.
items.body:
A working XSS sink can be proven with a payload that ships the victim's document.cookie to an attacker-controlled server, giving the tester an out-of-band confirmation rather than a visual alert.

HackTricks reference: 133098c3 (notion:133098c3-95c5-80b1-9bb1-f3a36d5d9adb)
items.disproof: The injected script never executes in a victim's browser session, or no request carrying the cookie ever reaches the attacker server.

items.claim: Any input field whose value is persisted and later rendered back into a page is a stored XSS candidate, so the test is to submit a marker payload and check whether it executes on a subsequent view of the page.
items.body:
Any input field whose value is persisted and later rendered back into a page is a stored XSS candidate, so the test is to submit a marker payload and check whether it executes on a subsequent view of the page.

HackTricks reference: 133098c3 (notion:133098c3-95c5-80b1-9bb1-f3a36d5d9adb)
items.disproof: The stored value is sanitized or escaped on render so the payload shows up as inert text on the next page view.
